entry.title: S.B. 53 — Transparency in Frontier AI Act (TFAIA)
entry.sponsor_text: Sen. Scott Wiener (D)
entry.mechanism: Frontier AI framework; transparency reports; critical-incident reporting 15 days, or 24 hrs if imminent risk of death/serious injury ; whistleblower protections incl. anonymous channel with monthly updates; annual definitional review; CalCompute consortium; preempts local ordinances adopted on/after Jan 1, 2025 regulating frontier catastrophic risk
entry.thresholds: 10²⁶ ops incl. fine-tuning/RL; "large frontier developer" = >$500M revenue; catastrophic risk = >50 deaths/serious injuries or >$1B damage
entry.penalties: Up to $1M/violation; AG enforcement; no general private right to enforce developer obligations, but employees may sue for whistleblower retaliation
entry.effective_text: Jan 1, 2026 (OES anonymized reporting & annual reviews from Jan 1, 2027)
entry.status_text: Signed: Sept 29, 2025 | Effective: Jan 1, 2026 (OES anonymized reporting & annual reviews from Jan 1, 2027)

events.text: Jan 1, 2026 (OES anonymized reporting & annual reviews from Jan 1, 2027)
events.clause: Jan 1, 2026 (OES anonymized reporting & annual reviews from Jan 1, 2027)

events.text: OES anonymized reporting & annual reviews begin Jan 1, 2027
events.clause: OES anonymized reporting & annual reviews begin Jan 1, 2027

framework.summary: Large frontier developers must write, follow and publish a frontier AI framework, and review it at least once a year.
framework.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework

transparency_report.summary: Every frontier developer must publish a transparency report when it deploys a new or substantially modified frontier model.
transparency_report.quote: a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a transparency report

incident_reporting.summary: Critical safety incidents must be reported to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovery.
incident_reporting.quote: shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovering the critical safety incident

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: An incident posing an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury must be disclosed to an appropriate authority within 24 hours.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within 24 hours

third_party_audit.summary: The framework must describe how the developer uses third parties to assess catastrophic risk; no independent audit is required.
third_party_audit.quote: Using third parties to assess the potential for catastrophic risks and the effectiveness of mitigations of catastrophic risks.

whistleblower.summary: Frontier developers may not block or retaliate against employees who report catastrophic-risk dangers or violations of the Act.
whistleblower.quote: A frontier developer shall not make, adopt, enforce, or enter into a rule, regulation, policy, or contract that prevents a covered employee from disclosing, or retaliates against a covered employee for disclosing

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is one trained with more than 10^26 operations, counting fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
compute_threshold.quote: trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer has annual gross revenues above $500,000,000, with its affiliates, in the preceding calendar year.
revenue_threshold.quote: annual gross revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) in the preceding calendar year

harm_threshold.summary: Catastrophic risk means death or serious injury to more than 50 people, or more than $1,000,000,000 in property damage, from a single incident.
harm_threshold.quote: more than 50 people or more than one billion dollars ($1,000,000,000) in damage to, or loss of, property arising from a single incident

penalties.summary: Civil penalty of up to $1,000,000 per violation, recovered only in a civil action by the Attorney General.
penalties.quote: does not exceed one million dollars ($1,000,000) per violation

effective_date.summary: The bill text states no effective date.

entry.title: RAISE Act — Chapter 699 of 2025 (S.6953-B/A.6453-B), repealed and replaced by Chapter 96 of 2026 (S.8828/A.9449)
entry.sponsor_text: Sen. Andrew Gounardes (D); Asm. Alex Bores (D)
entry.mechanism: Chapter 96 repeals the original Gen. Bus. Law Art. 44-B and enacts a new Art. 44-B (§§1420–1429) that copies TFAIA's frontier AI framework (§1421(1)) and transparency report (§1421(3)) — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; incident reporting 72 hrs to the DFS Office, 24 hrs to law enforcement if imminent risk (§1422(3)); quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries (§1422(2)); large-developer disclosure statement with 5%/50% beneficial owners, renewed every 2 years , pro-rata assessment, $1,000/day for non-filing (§1428); new office within Dept. of Financial Services with broad rulemaking authority incl. "additional reporting or publication requirements" (§1429); scope limited to models "developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York" (§1425); exempts accredited colleges/universities and the Empire AI Consortium (§1426); §1427(3) expressly preserves a developer's right to argue another party caused the harm. Federal reciprocity is narrower than IL's: it covers incident reporting only (§1422(8)–(9)). Contains no whistleblower section and no audit mandate — both were in the June 2025 version and were removed
entry.thresholds: 10²⁶ ops incl. fine-tuning/RL/material modifications (§1420(9)); >$500M revenue with affiliates, preceding calendar year (§1420(10)); catastrophic risk >50 deaths/serious injury or >$1B; catastrophic risk involves expert-level assistance in creating a chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear weapon, cyberattack or crime without meaningful human oversight, or evading developer control (§1420(3)(a)); equity-value loss excluded (§1423)
entry.penalties: $1M first / $3M subsequent violation, scaled to severity (AG civil action, §1427(1)) for unpublished/untransmitted compliant documents, false statements, unreported incidents, or breaching own framework; DFS office may, after notice and hearing, levy one thousand dollars per day for no disclosure statement or uncorrected false information, plus assessments owed (§1428(5)); no private right of action (§1427(2)); good-faith exception for false statements (§1421(4)(b))

entry.mechanism: Chapter 96 repeals the original Gen. Bus. Law Art. 44-B and enacts a new Art. 44-B (§§1420–1429) that copies TFAIA's frontier AI framework (§1421(1)) and transparency report (§1421(3)) — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; incident reporting 72 hrs to the DFS Office, 24 hrs to law enforcement if imminent risk (§1422(3)); quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries (§1422(2)); large-developer disclosure statement with 5%/50% beneficial owners, renewed every 2 years , pro-rata assessment, $1,000/day for non-filing (§1428); new office within Dept. of Financial Services with broad rulemaking authority incl. "additional reporting or publication requirements" (§1429); scope limited to models "developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York" (§1425); exempts accredited colleges/universities and the Empire AI Consortium (§1426); §1427(3) expressly preserves a developer's right to argue another party caused the harm. entry.penalties: $1M first / $3M subsequent violation, scaled to severity (AG civil action, §1427(1)) for unpublished/untransmitted compliant documents, false statements, unreported incidents, or breaching own framework; DFS office may, after notice and hearing, levy one thousand dollars per day for no disclosure statement or uncorrected false information, plus assessments owed (§1428(5)); no private right of action (§1427(2)); good-faith exception for false statements (§1421(4)(b))

entry.mechanism: Chapter 96 repeals the original Gen. Bus. Law Art. 44-B and enacts a new Art. 44-B (§§1420–1429) that copies TFAIA's frontier AI framework (§1421(1)) and transparency report (§1421(3)) — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; incident reporting 72 hrs to the DFS Office, 24 hrs to law enforcement if imminent risk (§1422(3)); quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries (§1422(2)); large-developer disclosure statement with 5%/50% beneficial owners, renewed every 2 years , pro-rata assessment, $1,000/day for non-filing (§1428); new office within Dept. of Financial Services with broad rulemaking authority incl. "additional reporting or publication requirements" (§1429); scope limited to models "developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York" (§1425); exempts accredited colleges/universities and the Empire AI Consortium (§1426); §1427(3) expressly preserves a developer's right to argue another party caused the harm. entry.title: RAISE Act — Chapter 699 of 2025 (S.6953-B/A.6453-B), repealed and replaced by Chapter 96 of 2026 (S.8828/A.9449)
entry.sponsor_text: Sen. Andrew Gounardes (D); Asm. Alex Bores (D)
entry.mechanism: Chapter 96 repeals the original Gen. Bus. Law Art. 44-B and enacts a new Art. 44-B (§§1420–1429) that copies TFAIA's frontier AI framework (§1421(1)) and transparency report (§1421(3)) — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; incident reporting 72 hrs to the DFS Office, 24 hrs to law enforcement if imminent risk (§1422(3)); quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries (§1422(2)); large-developer disclosure statement with 5%/50% beneficial owners, renewed every 2 years , pro-rata assessment, $1,000/day for non-filing (§1428); new office within Dept. of Financial Services with broad rulemaking authority incl. "additional reporting or publication requirements" (§1429); scope limited to models "developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York" (§1425); exempts accredited colleges/universities and the Empire AI Consortium (§1426); §1427(3) expressly preserves a developer's right to argue another party caused the harm. Federal reciprocity is narrower than IL's: it covers incident reporting only (§1422(8)–(9)). Contains no whistleblower section and no audit mandate — both were in the June 2025 version and were removed
entry.thresholds: 10²⁶ ops incl. fine-tuning/RL/material modifications (§1420(9)); >$500M revenue with affiliates, preceding calendar year (§1420(10)); catastrophic risk >50 deaths/serious injury or >$1B; catastrophic risk involves expert-level assistance in creating a chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear weapon, cyberattack or crime without meaningful human oversight, or evading developer control (§1420(3)(a)); equity-value loss excluded (§1423)
entry.penalties: $1M first / $3M subsequent violation, scaled to severity (AG civil action, §1427(1)) for unpublished/untransmitted compliant documents, false statements, unreported incidents, or breaching own framework; DFS office may, after notice and hearing, levy one thousand dollars per day for no disclosure statement or uncorrected false information, plus assessments owed (§1428(5)); no private right of action (§1427(2)); good-faith exception for false statements (§1421(4)(b))

entry.title: S.B. 315 — AI Safety Measures Act (Public Act 104-0538)
entry.sponsor_text: Sen. Mary Edly-Allen (D-Lake County), chief sponsor; Rep. Daniel Didech (D-Buffalo Grove), House; broadly bipartisan co-sponsors (chief co-sponsors include Republicans Rezin, Hills, Curran)
entry.mechanism: Sec. 10: frontier AI framework (from Jan 1, 2028); transparency reports before/at deployment — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; annual independent third-party audit (from Jan 1, 2028 or 90 days after qualifying), auditor must have no financial interest in developer and payment can't be conditioned on results; redacted audit report published within 30 days and sent to Agency + AG; quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries. Sec. 15: incident reporting 72 hrs to Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security ("Agency") + AG; 24 hrs to appropriate authority if imminent risk of death/serious injury; public reporting mechanism; FOIA exemption for incident reports, internal-use assessments, unredacted audits, auditor work papers. Sec. 17 interoperability: developer may declare intent to comply via a designated federal law/regulation/guidance that (1) has substantially equivalent-or-stricter incident reporting, (3) is substantially equivalent in mitigating catastrophic risk, and (4) requires independent third-party audits — then failure to meet the federal standard is an IL violation. Sec. 18: disclosure statement with 5%+ beneficial owners (private) / 50%+ (public), renewed annually, pro-rata fee. Sec. 20: whistleblower protections for "covered employees" incl. anonymous channel with monthly updates and AG Workplace Rights Hotline; amends IL Whistleblower Act. Sec. 35: declares frontier-model regulation an exclusive State power — denies home rule . Legislative mechanics: introduced Jan 24, 2025 as a Predatory Loan Prevention Act technical bill; Senate Floor Amendment No. 1 (filed May 11, 2026) replaced the entire text; four floor amendments adopted May 21. Timing mismatch worth flagging: Sec. 10(c) transparency reports have no 2028 gate and so apply from the Jan 1, 2027 effective date, yet large-developer reports must summarize assessments "conducted pursuant to the frontier AI framework" — which isn't required until 2028
entry.thresholds: 10²⁶ ops incl. original run + fine-tuning/RL/material modifications; "large frontier developer" = >$500M revenue with affiliates, preceding calendar year; catastrophic risk = >50 deaths/serious injury or >$1B (equity-value loss excluded, Sec. 25(c))
entry.penalties: $1M first / $3M subsequent, scaled to severity; AG-exclusive action under the AI Act; no general private right under that Act, but employee remedies are preserved through the Illinois Whistleblower Act; $1,000/day (Agency, after notice and hearing) for failing to file a disclosure statement or correct false information, plus assessments owed; good-faith exception for false statements (Sec. 10(f)(2))

transparency_report.summary: Every frontier developer must publish a transparency report before or when it deploys a new or substantially modified frontier model; large developers add machine-readable risk summaries.
transparency_report.quote: a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a transparency report containing all of the following

incident_reporting.summary: Frontier developers must report each critical safety incident to the state emergency agency and the Attorney General within 72 hours of reasonably believing one occurred.
incident_reporting.quote: within 72 hours of the frontier developer learning facts sufficient to establish a reasonable belief that a critical safety incident has occurred

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: An incident posing imminent risk of death or serious physical injury must be disclosed within 24 hours to an appropriate authority such as law enforcement.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within 24 hours

third_party_audit.summary: Beginning January 1, 2028, large frontier developers must each year hire an independent third party to audit compliance, then publish a summary and the redacted report within 30 days.
third_party_audit.quote: a large frontier developer shall annually retain a third party to perform an independent audit of compliance with the requirements of this Section

whistleblower.summary: Frontier developers may not block or retaliate against covered employees who report catastrophic-risk dangers or violations of the Act, and must give notice of those rights.
whistleblower.quote: A frontier developer shall not make, adopt, enforce, or enter into a rule, regulation, policy, or contract that prevents a covered employee from disclosing

registration.summary: Beginning January 1, 2027, large frontier developers may not develop, deploy or operate a frontier model in Illinois without a current disclosure statement on file with the Agency and fees paid.
registration.quote: no large frontier developer may develop, deploy, or operate a frontier model, in whole or in part in this State, without having a current disclosure statement filed with the Agency and paying the required fee

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is a foundation model trained with computing power greater than 1026 (as printed) integer or floating-point operations, including fine-tuning.
compute_threshold.quote: using a quantity of computing power greater than 1026 integer or floating-point operations

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer, with its affiliates, had annual gross revenues above $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year.
revenue_threshold.quote: collectively had annual gross revenues in excess of $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year

harm_threshold.summary: Catastrophic risk means death or serious injury to more than 50 people, or more than $1,000,000,000 in property damage, from a single incident.
harm_threshold.quote: more than 50 people or more than $1,000,000,000 in damage to, or loss of, property arising from a single incident

penalties.summary: Attorney General civil action: up to $1,000,000 for a first violation and $3,000,000 for later ones (Sec. 25); the Agency may separately fine $1,000 a day for a missing disclosure (Sec. 18(e)).
penalties.quote: the civil penalty may not exceed $3,000,000 per violation

effective_date.summary: The Act takes effect January 41, 2027 as printed in the stored text (a likely typo); the framework and audit duties begin January 1, 2028.
effective_date.quote: This Act takes effect January 41, 2027.

draft.summary_line: Would require large frontier AI developers to publish safety frameworks, report critical incidents and undergo independent audits, with Attorney General enforcement.

entry.title: H.5576 — "An Act relative to economic development in the commonwealth" (Senate AI language = amendment S.3178; lineage: S.37 → S.2630 → S.3178)

entry.mechanism: Frontier AI framework; risk reports every 180 days; critical safety incidents reported to AG within 15 days (24 hours if imminent risk of death); annual independent third-party audit; AG civil-action enforcement, up to $1,000,000 first violation, $3,000,000 subsequent; Senate version: mandatory independent third-party catastrophic-risk review at least every 120 days (the most frequent evaluation cadence among the bills reviewed); whistleblower protections (covered employees may petition superior court for injunctive relief; court may award attorney's fees and court costs to a successful plaintiff); commission on further AI regulation. Chapter 93M effective July 1, 2027. House version (passed July 8) contains no AI-safety language — only funding.
entry.thresholds: Senate text: frontier model = foundation model trained using >10^26 integer or floating-point operations (including fine-tuning and other modifications); large frontier developer = >$500,000,000 annual gross revenues together with affiliates; catastrophic risk 50+ deaths or $1B
entry.status_text: Status (as of Sept 5, 2026): [PENDING] House passed 148-2 July 8; Senate struck all after the enacting clause and inserted S.3178 text July 24 (reprinted as S.3228); House non-concurred July 30; conference committee appointed July 30 (Senate: Finegold-Rodrigues-Durant; House: Michlewitz-Fiola-Soter). Official bill history checked live Sept 4, 2026: no action since July 30. Formal session ended July 31; informal sessions can still act but can't override a veto. Not enacted. Bill history re-checked Sept 28, 2026: still no action since July 30. OpenAI lobbying for IL-style annual audits; Anthropic for the stronger Rush amendment. Earlier House text: the Joint Committee on Economic Development and Emerging Technologies reported H.5527 on June 22, 2026 (its redraft of the Governor's H.5386), which included a Chapter 93M "Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act" (frontier model trained on more than 10^26 operations). S.3224 (Sen. Rush, filed July 23, 2026) is a floor amendment to the Senate Ways and Means text S.3178, not a separate bill; whether it was adopted could not be confirmed

framework.summary: Large frontier developers must write, follow and publish a frontier AI framework, and review it at least annually.
framework.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with and clearly

transparency_report.summary: Every frontier developer must publish a transparency report when it deploys a new or substantially modified model; large developers must also publish a catastrophic-risk report updated every 180 days.
transparency_report.quote: conspicuously publish on its website a transparency report containing

incident_reporting.summary: Critical safety incidents must be reported to the Attorney General within 15 days of discovery.
incident_reporting.quote: of its frontier models to the attorney general within 15 days of discovering the critical safety

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: An incident posing an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury must be disclosed to an appropriate authority within 24 hours.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: that incident within 24 hours to an authority, including any law enforcement agency or public

third_party_audit.summary: Large frontier developers must each year retain an independent third party to audit compliance, and engage an independent evaluator of catastrophic risk at least every 120 days.
third_party_audit.quote: A large frontier developer shall annually retain a third party to perform an

whistleblower.summary: Frontier developers may not block or retaliate against employees who report catastrophic-risk dangers or violations; large developers need an internal reporting process with monthly updates.
whistleblower.quote: regulation, policy or contract that prevents a covered employee from disclosing or retaliates

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement for developers.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is one trained with more than 10^26 operations, counting fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
compute_threshold.quote: power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer, with its affiliates, has annual gross revenues above $500,000,000.
revenue_threshold.quote: collectively has annual gross revenues greater than $500,000,000

harm_threshold.summary: Catastrophic risk means death or serious injury to at least 50 people, or at least $1,000,000,000 in property damage, from a single incident.
harm_threshold.quote: death of, or serious injury to, not less than 50 people or not less than $1,000,000,000 in damage

penalties.summary: Civil penalty up to $1,000,000 for a first violation and $3,000,000 for later ones, recovered only by the Attorney General in a civil action.
penalties.quote: $1,000,000 for a first violation and not more than $3,000,000 for subsequent violations

effective_date.summary: Chapter 93M takes effect July 1, 2027 (Sec. 355). Secs. 346-347 date the annual audit and 120-day evaluation from January 1, 2027 or 180 days after qualifying, whichever is later, which conflicts with Sec. 355.
effective_date.quote: 93M of the General Laws shall take effect on July 1, 2027.

thirty_seconds.a: Frontier AI developers training models with more than 10^26 operations; "large" developers have over $500,000,000 in annual gross revenues with affiliates. Fines reach $7,777,777.
thirty_seconds.b: Publish a safety framework and risk reports every 180 days, report critical safety incidents to the Attorney General within 15 days, and get an annual independent audit.
thirty_seconds.c: The Attorney General can bring a civil action for up to $1,000,000 for a first violation and $3,000,000 for later ones.

entry.title: H.B. 4668 — Artificial Intelligence Safety and Security Transparency Act
entry.sponsor_text: Rep. Lightner (R)
entry.mechanism: Safety & security protocol; transparency reports every 90 days ; annual third-party audit (published within 90 days); whistleblower protections with private right of action (90-day window, clear-and-convincing standard) + anonymous channel with monthly updates; AG enforcement with civil fines up to $1,000,000 per violation (and up to $500 under one section). Appears to be a clone of the original June 2025 RAISE Act text — same $5M/$100M compute-cost thresholds, same 100-death threshold, same audit/whistleblower structure that NY later stripped out. Effective dates are written as "Beginning January 1, 2026" — already past, since the bill hasn't moved
entry.thresholds: Cost-based, not FLOP-based: "large developer" = trained a model costing ≥$5M in compute (at prevailing cloud prices) and ≥$100M aggregate compute cost in preceding 12 months; critical risk = >100 deaths/serious injuries or >$1B

framework.summary: Large developers must produce, follow and publish a safety and security protocol, and publish changes within 30 days.
framework.quote: Produce, implement, follow, and conspicuously publish a safety and security protocol.

transparency_report.summary: Large developers must publish a transparency report on risk assessments at least once every 90 days.
transparency_report.quote: Not less than once every 90 days, produce and conspicuously publish a transparency report

incident_reporting.summary: The protocol must state when and to whom the developer will report incidents; the bill sets no reporting duty or deadline itself.
incident_reporting.quote: The conditions under which the large developer will report an incident relevant to a critical risk

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no shorter reporting window for imminent risks.

third_party_audit.summary: Large developers must hire a reputable third-party auditor at least once per year to assess protocol compliance, and publish the report.
third_party_audit.quote: not less than once per year, a large developer shall retain a reputable third-party auditor to produce a report

whistleblower.summary: Large developers may not retaliate against employees who report critical risks to authorities; employees may sue.
whistleblower.quote: A large developer shall not discharge, threaten, or otherwise discriminate against an employee

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: Coverage is set by the cost of training compute ($5,000,000.00 for one model), not by operations count.
compute_threshold.quote: model with a quantity of computing power that costs not less than $5,000,000.00

revenue_threshold.summary: No revenue test; a large developer also needs $100,000,000.00 of compute spending on models in the prior 12 months.
revenue_threshold.quote: total quantity of computing power that costs not less than $100,000,000.00

harm_threshold.summary: Critical risk means death or serious injury to more than 100 people, or more than $1,000,000,000.00 in damages, from listed incident kinds.
harm_threshold.quote: more than 100 people, or will result in more than $1,000,000,000.00 in damages to rights in money or property

penalties.summary: The Attorney General may sue for a civil fine up to $1,000,000.00 per violation of the publication, reporting and audit duties (Sec. 7 and 9), plus injunctive relief; whistleblower violations carry a fine up to $500.00.
penalties.quote: A civil fine of not more than $1,000,000.00 per violation.

framework.summary: Large developers must produce, follow and publish a safety and security protocol, and publish changes within 30 days.
framework.quote: Produce, implement, follow, and conspicuously publish a safety and security protocol.

transparency_report.summary: Large developers must publish a transparency report on risk assessments at least once every 90 days.
transparency_report.quote: Not less than once every 90 days, produce and conspicuously publish a transparency report

incident_reporting.summary: The protocol must state when and to whom the developer will report incidents; the bill sets no reporting duty or deadline itself.
incident_reporting.quote: The conditions under which the large developer will report an incident relevant to a critical risk

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no shorter reporting window for imminent risks.

third_party_audit.summary: Large developers must hire a reputable third-party auditor at least once per year to assess protocol compliance, and publish the report.
third_party_audit.quote: not less than once per year, a large developer shall retain a reputable third-party auditor to produce a report

whistleblower.summary: Large developers may not retaliate against employees who report critical risks to authorities; employees may sue.

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: Coverage is set by the cost of training compute ($5,000,000.00 for one model), not by operations count.
compute_threshold.quote: model with a quantity of computing power that costs not less than $5,000,000.00

revenue_threshold.summary: No revenue test; a large developer also needs $100,000,000.00 of compute spending on models in the prior 12 months.
revenue_threshold.quote: total quantity of computing power that costs not less than $100,000,000.00

harm_threshold.summary: Critical risk means death or serious injury to more than 100 people, or more than $1,000,000,000.00 in damages, from listed incident kinds.
harm_threshold.quote: more than 100 people, or will result in more than $1,000,000,000.00 in damages to rights in money or property

penalties.summary: The Attorney General may sue for a civil fine up to $1,000,000.00 per violation of the publication, reporting and audit duties (Sec. 7 and 9), plus injunctive relief; whistleblower violations carry a fine up to $500.00.
penalties.quote: A civil fine of not more than $1,000,000.00 per violation.

framework.summary: Large developers must produce, follow and publish a safety and security protocol, and publish changes within 30 days.
framework.quote: Produce, implement, follow, and conspicuously publish a safety and security protocol.

transparency_report.summary: Large developers must publish a transparency report on risk assessments at least once every 90 days.
transparency_report.quote: Not less than once every 90 days, produce and conspicuously publish a transparency report

incident_reporting.summary: The protocol must state when and to whom the developer will report incidents; the bill sets no reporting duty or deadline itself.
incident_reporting.quote: The conditions under which the large developer will report an incident relevant to a critical risk

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no shorter reporting window for imminent risks.

third_party_audit.summary: Large developers must hire a reputable third-party auditor at least once per year to assess protocol compliance, and publish the report.
third_party_audit.quote: not less than once per year, a large developer shall retain a reputable third-party auditor to produce a report

whistleblower.summary: Large developers may not retaliate against employees who report critical risks to authorities; employees may sue.
whistleblower.quote: A large developer shall not discharge, threaten, or otherwise discriminate against an employee

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: Coverage is set by the cost of training compute ($5,000,000.00 for one model), not by operations count.
compute_threshold.quote: model with a quantity of computing power that costs not less than $5,000,000.00

revenue_threshold.summary: No revenue test; a large developer also needs $100,000,000.00 of compute spending on models in the prior 12 months.
revenue_threshold.quote: total quantity of computing power that costs not less than $100,000,000.00

harm_threshold.summary: Critical risk means death or serious injury to more than 100 people, or more than $1,000,000,000.00 in damages, from listed incident kinds.
harm_threshold.quote: more than 100 people, or will result in more than $1,000,000,000.00 in damages to rights in money or property

penalties.summary: The Attorney General may sue for a civil fine up to $1,000,000.00 per violation of the publication, reporting and audit duties (Sec. 7 and 9), plus injunctive relief; whistleblower violations carry a fine up to $500.00.
penalties.quote: A civil fine of not more than $1,000,000.00 per violation.

effective_date.summary: The developer duties begin on January 1, 2026.
effective_date.quote: Beginning on January 1, 2026, a large developer shall do all of the following

thirty_seconds.a: The entry text does not say who is covered.
thirty_seconds.b: Publish a safety and security protocol, publish a transparency report at least once every 90 days, and hire a third-party auditor at least once per year.

entry.title: H.B. 4668 — Artificial Intelligence Safety and Security Transparency Act
entry.sponsor_text: Rep. Lightner (R)
entry.mechanism: Safety & security protocol; transparency reports every 90 days ; annual third-party audit (published within 90 days); whistleblower protections with private right of action (90-day window, clear-and-convincing standard) + anonymous channel with monthly updates; AG enforcement with civil fines up to $1,000,000 per violation (and up to $500 under one section). Appears to be a clone of the original June 2025 RAISE Act text — same $5M/$100M compute-cost thresholds, same 100-death threshold, same audit/whistleblower structure that NY later stripped out. Effective dates are written as "Beginning January 1, 2026" — already past, since the bill hasn't moved
entry.thresholds: Cost-based, not FLOP-based: "large developer" = trained a model costing ≥$5M in compute (at prevailing cloud prices) and ≥$100M aggregate compute cost in preceding 12 months; critical risk = >100 deaths/serious injuries or >$1B

entry.title: H.B. 4668 — Artificial Intelligence Safety and Security Transparency Act
entry.sponsor_text: Rep. Lightner (R)
entry.mechanism: Safety & security protocol; transparency reports every 90 days ; annual third-party audit (published within 90 days); whistleblower protections with private right of action (90-day window, clear-and-convincing standard) + anonymous channel with monthly updates; AG enforcement with civil fines up to $1,000,000 per violation (and up to $500 under one section). Appears to be a clone of the original June 2025 RAISE Act text — same $5M/$100M compute-cost thresholds, same 100-death threshold, same audit/whistleblower structure that NY later stripped out. Effective dates are written as "Beginning January 1, 2026" — already past, since the bill hasn't moved
entry.thresholds: Cost-based, not FLOP-based: "large developer" = trained a model costing ≥$5M in compute (at prevailing cloud prices) and ≥$100M aggregate compute cost in preceding 12 months; critical risk = >100 deaths/serious injuries or >$1B

entry.mechanism: Large frontier developers with NJ users must: implement protocols; file annual "Risk Management Disclosure" with AG, mapped item-by-item to the NIST AI RMF ; file pre-deployment "New Model Risk Disclosure" with replicable assessments; flag which sections were written by generative AI . AG publishes with redactions; civil penalty of $100,000 per violation. AG may audit or contract a private auditor (discretionary). 5-year sunset. Defines "critical safety incident" but imposes no reporting obligation (orphaned definition). No whistleblower provisions
entry.thresholds: 10²⁶ ops incl. fine-tuning/RL; "large frontier developer" = >$100M revenue (lowest of any bill); catastrophic harm = 25+ deaths/serious injuries or $1B (lowest casualty threshold of any bill); weapons list includes illegal firearms, lethal autonomous weapons, explosives — broader than CBRN

events.clause: referred to Assembly Science, Innovation & Technology Committee. S.4446 introduced June 11, 2026 — identical text (verified against njleg.gov)

events.clause: \[PENDING\] A.5275 introduced June 15, 2026

framework.summary: Large frontier developers with New Jersey users must write and implement risk protocols and review them yearly.
framework.quote: write and implement technical and organizational protocols to assess and reduce the risk

transparency_report.summary: Developers must file a yearly Risk Management Disclosure and a New Model Risk Disclosure with the Attorney General, who publishes them.
transparency_report.quote: annually submit to the Attorney General a "Risk Management Disclosure"

incident_reporting.summary: The bill requires no incident reporting.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no imminent-risk reporting window.

third_party_audit.summary: The Attorney General may audit developers or hire a private auditor; developers themselves need not obtain an audit.
third_party_audit.quote: enter into a contract with a private entity to conduct an audit

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no whistleblower protection.

registration.summary: Developers must file a New Model Risk Disclosure with the Attorney General before or when deploying a new model; this is notice, not a licence.
registration.quote: before, or concurrently with, deploying a new frontier model

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier developer used at least 10^26 integer or floating-point operations to train a frontier model.
compute_threshold.quote: a quantity of computing power of at least 10^26 integer or floating-point operations to train a frontier model

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer, with affiliates, had annual gross revenues above $100 million in the preceding calendar year.
revenue_threshold.quote: annual gross revenues in excess of $100 million in the preceding calendar year

harm_threshold.summary: Catastrophic harm means death or serious injury of 25 or more people, or $1 billion in property damage, from a single incident.
harm_threshold.quote: death or serious injury of 25 or more people or $1 billion in damage to, or loss of, property arising from a single incident

penalties.summary: $100,000 civil penalty per violation for missing or materially false disclosures, collected by the Attorney General; no penalty for a materially false statement made in good faith and reasonable (Sec. 4(b)).
penalties.quote: shall be liable for a civil penalty in the amount of $100,000 for each violation

effective_date.summary: Takes effect six months after enactment; sections 1 through 6 expire five years later.
effective_date.quote: This act shall take effect six months after the date of enactment.

thirty_seconds.a: Large frontier developers with New Jersey users, meaning those with more than $100 million in annual gross revenues that train models using at least 10^26 operations.
thirty_seconds.b: Implement risk protocols, file a yearly Risk Management Disclosure, and file a New Model Risk Disclosure before or when deploying a new frontier model.
thirty_seconds.c: A civil penalty of $100,000 per violation, collected by the Attorney General, who may also audit developers or hire a private auditor.

entry.title: H.B. 3506 — Artificial Intelligence Safety and Security Protocol Act (2025)
entry.sponsor_text: Rep. Daniel Didech (D); co-sponsor Rep. Matt Hanson (added Jan. 2026)
entry.mechanism: The FPF-counted 2025 Illinois frontier bill — gap resolved. Original-RAISE-style design, the same template as MI H.B. 4668: developers publish a safety and security protocol; risk assessment report every 90 days ; annual third-party audit of protocol compliance; redaction rules; whistleblower protections (Committee Amendment No. 1 narrowed scope to "large developer" and added employee civil damages); civil penalties. Illinois lineage: this 2025 SSP bill did not advance; the 2026 S.B. 3312/S.B. 315 switched to the TFAIA template and added the audit back — the state moved from the original-RAISE structure to California-plus-audits within twelve months
entry.thresholds: Floor Amendment No. 2: "large developer" = ≥$5M compute cost for a single model and ≥$100M aggregate compute cost over the preceding 12 months — the original-RAISE test. As introduced: "developer" = trained at least one foundation model with compute costing at least $100,000,000 at cloud market prices; critical risk = >100 deaths/serious injuries or >$1,000,000,000 damage
entry.status_text: Status (as of Sept 5, 2026): [STALLED] Filed Feb. 7, 2025; passed Cybersecurity, Data Analytics & IT Committee 7–4 (Mar. 20, 2025) ; held on second reading; re-referred to Rules under Rule 19(a) Apr. 11, 2025 . Inactive, but not formally dead while the 104th General Assembly remains open

framework.summary: A developer must produce, follow and publish a safety and security protocol, and publish any material change within 30 days.
framework.quote: A developer shall produce, implement, follow, and conspicuously publish a safety and security protocol.

transparency_report.summary: A developer must publish a risk assessment report at least every 90 days.
transparency_report.quote: No less than every 90 days, a developer shall produce and conspicuously publish a risk assessment report.

incident_reporting.summary: The protocol must state when and to whom the developer will report incidents; the bill sets no reporting window or government recipient.
incident_reporting.quote: the conditions under which the developer will report incidents relevant to critical risk that have occurred in connection with one or more of its foundation models

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no imminent-risk reporting window.

third_party_audit.summary: At least once a year a developer must hire a reputable third-party auditor to assess its compliance with its protocol, and publish the report within 90 days.
third_party_audit.quote: At least once every calendar year, a developer shall retain a reputable third-party auditor to produce a report assessing the following

whistleblower.summary: The Whistleblower Act applies to employees who tell the Attorney General about critical risk, and developers must offer an anonymous internal reporting process.
whistleblower.quote: A developer shall provide a reasonable internal process through which an employee may anonymously disclose information to the developer

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A developer is covered by compute cost, not operation count: training a model with computing power costing at least $100,000,000.
compute_threshold.quote: has trained at least one foundation model with a quantity of computational power that costs at least $100,000,000

revenue_threshold.summary: A developer is covered by spending: it has trained a model with computing power costing at least $100,000,000; no revenue or user test.
revenue_threshold.quote: has trained at least one foundation model with a quantity of computational power that costs at least $100,000,000

harm_threshold.summary: Critical risk means a foreseeable risk of death or serious injury to more than 100 people, or more than $1,000,000,000 in damage.
harm_threshold.quote: will result in the death of, or serious injury to, more than 100 people, or more than $1,000,000,000 in damage to rights in money or property

penalties.summary: The Attorney General may sue for civil penalties up to $1,000,000 for violating Sec. 15 or 25, and seek injunctive or declaratory relief.
penalties.quote: may be assessed a civil penalty not to exceed $1,000,000

effective_date.summary: The bill text states no effective date.

entry.thresholds: Frontier models defined by compute or cost: trained using greater than 10^26 computational operations, or compute cost that exceeds $100,000,000; critical harm = death or serious injury of 100 or more people or at least $1,000,000,000 of property damages
entry.status_text: Status (as of Sept 5, 2026): [STALLED] Introduced Feb 4, 2026; re-referred to Assignments May 22, 2026 (stalled) — superseded politically by SB 315

events.text: \[STALLED\] Introduced Feb 4, 2026
events.clause: \[STALLED\] Introduced Feb 4, 2026

events.text: re-referred to Assignments May 22, 2026 (stalled) — superseded politically by SB 315
events.clause: re-referred to Assignments May 22, 2026 (stalled) — superseded politically by SB 315

framework.summary: A developer that publishes and follows a safety and security protocol is shielded from liability for critical harms; publishing is a condition of that shield, not a flat duty.
framework.quote: published a safety and security protocol on its website that satisfies the requirements of Section

transparency_report.summary: A developer must publish a transparency report at release to get the liability shield; it is a condition of the shield, not a flat mandate.
transparency_report.quote: published a transparency report on its website at the time of the frontier model's release

incident_reporting.summary: The bill requires no incident reporting.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no imminent-risk reporting window.

third_party_audit.summary: The protocol must say whether and how the developer uses third parties to assess risk; no independent audit is required.
third_party_audit.quote: whether and how a developer will use third parties to assess risk of critical harm

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no whistleblower protection.

registration.summary: A developer relying on a federal agency agreement must file a certification with the Attorney General; no pre-development registration is required.
registration.quote: shall file a certification with the Attorney General, in a manner prescribed by the Attorney General

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is one trained with more than 10^26 operations, or with a compute cost above $100,000,000.
compute_threshold.quote: is trained using greater than 10^26 computational operations

revenue_threshold.summary: A frontier model can also be defined by compute cost exceeding $100,000,000.
revenue_threshold.quote: has a compute cost that exceeds $100,000,000

harm_threshold.summary: Critical harm means death or serious injury of 100 or more people, or at least $1,000,000,000 in property damage.
harm_threshold.quote: the death or serious injury of 100 or more people or at least $1,000,000,000 of damages to rights in property

penalties.summary: The bill states no fine or enforcement remedy; it only removes liability for critical harms when conditions are met, and calls a false certification a violation without a stated penalty.

effective_date.summary: The bill text states no effective date.

draft.summary_line: Would have required large frontier AI developers to publish safety frameworks and report critical incidents, with civil penalties up to $1,000,000 per violation.

entry.title: H.B. 4705 — AI Public Safety and Child Protection Transparency Act
entry.sponsor_text: Rep. Daniel Didech (D); Senate parallel S.B. 3261 , sponsored by Sen. Mary Edly-Allen (D) and co-sponsors ( ILGA )
entry.mechanism: Hybrid: frontier developers and large chatbot providers must publish a public-safety and child-protection plan; AG incident-reporting mechanism; frontier developers must report critical safety incidents to the AG within 15 days, or within 24 hours to an appropriate authority if imminent risk of death or serious physical injury; chatbot providers report child safety incidents to AG within 15 days; plan modifications published within 30 days; whistleblower protections; annual third-party audits of large frontier developers; AG rulemaking; civil penalties up to $1,000,000 per violation (frontier developers) and $50,000 per violation (large chatbot providers); large frontier developer shall not use or deploy a frontier model if doing so would pose unreasonable catastrophic risk
entry.thresholds: 10²⁶ ops (computing for original training run plus any subsequent fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or other material modifications); large frontier developer = ≥$500M annual revenue including affiliates; large chatbot provider = ≥$25M annual revenue including affiliates; a covered chatbot must also have ≥1M monthly active users and be foreseeably accessible by minors

framework.summary: Large frontier developers and large chatbot providers must write, follow and publish a public safety and child protection plan.
framework.quote: shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a public safety and child protection plan

transparency_report.summary: Before deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model, a large frontier developer must publish summaries of its risk assessments and results.
transparency_report.quote: conspicuously publish on its website summaries of the following

incident_reporting.summary: Frontier developers must report critical safety incidents to the Attorney General within 15 days of discovery.
incident_reporting.quote: A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one of its frontier models to the Attorney General within 15 days after discovering the critical safety incident.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: A critical incident posing imminent risk of death or serious physical injury must be disclosed to an appropriate authority within 24 hours.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within 24 hours

third_party_audit.summary: Large frontier developers must hire a reputable third-party auditor every calendar year to assess compliance with their plan.
third_party_audit.quote: At least once every calendar year, a large frontier developer shall retain a reputable third-party auditor to produce a report

whistleblower.summary: Developers may not block protected disclosures by employees, and large frontier developers must offer an anonymous internal reporting process.
whistleblower.quote: shall not make, adopt, enforce, or enter into a rule, regulation, policy, or contract that prevents an employee from making a disclosure protected under the Whistleblower Act

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is one trained with more than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations, including fine-tuning.
compute_threshold.quote: trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer (with affiliates) has annual revenue of at least $500,000,000; a large chatbot provider, at least $25,000,000.
revenue_threshold.quote: collectively have an annual revenue of at least $500,000,000

harm_threshold.summary: A critical safety incident includes death or serious injury to more than 50 people, or more than $1,000,000,000 in property damage, from a catastrophic risk.
harm_threshold.quote: more than 50 people or more than $1,000,000,000 in damage to, or loss of, property

penalties.summary: Civil penalty up to $1,000,000 per violation for large frontier developers ($50,000 for chatbot providers), recovered by the Attorney General.
penalties.quote: does not exceed $1,000,000 per violation

effective_date.summary: Takes effect in 2027; the stored text reads garbled as January 231, 2027.
effective_date.quote: This Act takes effect January 231, 2027.

thirty_seconds.a: The entry text does not say who is covered.
thirty_seconds.b: Would require a published safety plan and incident reports to the Attorney General within 15 days. Imminent risk of death or serious injury would need disclosure within 24 hours. Large developers would need yearly audits.
thirty_seconds.c: Civil penalties up to $1,000,000 per violation for frontier developers and $50,000 for large chatbot providers. The bill is stalled in committee.

entry.mechanism: TFAIA-style public-safety plan plus a child-protection plan for covered chatbots; predeployment risk-assessment summaries; safety-incident reporting 15 days / 24 hrs if imminent to the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy or appropriate public-safety authority; quarterly internal-use summaries; false-statement prohibition; anonymous internal reporting and employee anti-retaliation remedies. AG enforcement; $1M first / $3M subsequent civil penalties
entry.thresholds: 10²⁶ ops; large frontier developer = ≥$500M annual revenue; catastrophic risk = >50 deaths/serious injuries or >$1B property loss; covered chatbot = ≥1M monthly active users and foreseeable access by minors
entry.status_text: Status (as of Sept 5, 2026): [FAILED] Introduced Jan. 19, 2026; first substitute received an 8–0 favorable committee recommendation Jan. 27; moved from the third-reading calendar to Rules Mar. 3; enacting clause struck and filed among bills not passed Mar. 6

events.clause: enacting clause struck and filed among bills not passed Mar. 6

framework.summary: Large frontier developers must write, follow and publish a public safety plan, and a child protection plan if they run a covered chatbot.
framework.quote: shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on the large frontier developer's internet website a public safety plan

transparency_report.summary: Before deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model, a large frontier developer must publish summaries of its risk assessments.
transparency_report.quote: A large frontier developer shall conspicuously publish on the large frontier developer's website summaries of the following before deploying a new frontier model

incident_reporting.summary: Large frontier developers must report a safety incident to the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy within 15 days of discovery.
incident_reporting.quote: A large frontier developer shall report a safety incident to the office within 15 days after the day on which the large frontier developer discovers the incident.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: A critical incident posing imminent risk of death or serious physical injury must be disclosed to law enforcement or a public safety agency within 24 hours.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, shall disclose that incident within 24

third_party_audit.summary: The plan must describe how the developer uses third parties to assess catastrophic risk; no independent audit is required.
third_party_audit.quote: uses third parties to assess the potential for catastrophic risks and the effectiveness of mitigations of catastrophic risks

whistleblower.summary: Frontier developers may not take adverse action against employees who report safety threats or violations; employees may sue.
whistleblower.quote: A frontier developer may not take adverse action against an employee because of a lawful act of the employee

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier developer has used at least 10^26 integer or floating-point operations to train a frontier model, including fine-tuning.
compute_threshold.quote: a quantity of computing power of at least 10^26 integer or floating-point operations to train a frontier model

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer, with affiliates, had annual revenue of at least $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year.
revenue_threshold.quote: had annual revenue of at least $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year

harm_threshold.summary: Catastrophic loss means death or serious bodily injury of more than 50 individuals, or property damage over $1,000,000,000.
harm_threshold.quote: the death or serious bodily injury of more than 50 individuals

penalties.summary: Civil penalty up to $1,000,000 for a first violation and $3,000,000 for each later one, sued for by the attorney general.
penalties.quote: A large frontier developer that violates this part is subject to a civil penalty that does not

effective_date.summary: The bill takes effect on May 6, 2026.
effective_date.quote: This bill takes effect on May 6, 2026.

draft.summary_line: Describes would have required large frontier AI developers to publish safety plans, report safety incidents, and protect whistleblowers, but the bill failed in March 2026.

framework.summary: Large frontier developers must write, follow and publish a frontier AI framework and review it at least once a year.
framework.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework

transparency_report.summary: Frontier developers must publish a transparency report before or when deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model; large developers add risk assessment summaries.
transparency_report.quote: a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a transparency report

incident_reporting.summary: Frontier developers must report critical safety incidents to the Department of Justice within 15 days of discovery.
incident_reporting.quote: to the department within fifteen days after discovering the critical safety incident

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: Incidents posing imminent risk of death, serious injury or an active cyberattack on critical infrastructure must be disclosed within 24 hours.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: poses an imminent risk of death, serious physical injury, or an active cyberattack on critical infrastructure, the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within twenty-four hours

third_party_audit.summary: From July 1, 2028, large frontier developers must hire an independent auditor each year to certify compliance with their framework and publish a summary within 30 days.
third_party_audit.quote: a large frontier developer shall retain a third-party auditor to produce a report signed

whistleblower.summary: Frontier developers may not block or retaliate against covered employees who report catastrophic risk or violations; large developers need an anonymous internal reporting process.
whistleblower.quote: enter into any policy or contract that prevents a covered employee from, or retaliates against a covered employee for, making a protected disclosure

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is one trained with more than 10^26 operations, including fine-tuning, or distilled from one at a compute cost over $5,000,000.
compute_threshold.quote: Was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer, with its affiliates, had more than five hundred million dollars in annual gross revenues in the preceding calendar year.
revenue_threshold.quote: had more than five hundred million dollars in annual gross

harm_threshold.summary: Catastrophic risk means death or serious injury of more than 50 people or more than $1,000,000,000 in property damage from a single incident.
harm_threshold.quote: the death or serious injury of more than fifty

penalties.summary: The Attorney General may sue large frontier developers for civil penalties up to $1,000,000 for a first violation and $10,000,000 for later violations of the same requirement.
penalties.quote: a penalty not to exceed one million dollars per violation for a first violation or ten million dollars for a second or subsequent violation of the same requirement

effective_date.summary: The Act becomes effective on January 1, 2027.
effective_date.quote: This Act shall become effective on January 1, 2027.

draft.summary_line: Would have made developers of covered AI models strictly liable for injuries to non-users caused by model conduct that would be negligent, tortious, or criminal if done by a human.

entry.title: S.358 / H.5224
entry.sponsor_text: Sen. Gu + 8 co-sponsors (S.358, Feb 21, 2025)
entry.mechanism: Different design: strict tort liability. Developers of covered models are strictly liable for injuries to non-users caused by model conduct that would be negligent, tortious, or criminal if done by a human, where the conduct was not intended or reasonably anticipated by the user or any fine-tuner; rebuttable presumption that the AI satisfies a tort's mental-state element ("it shall not be a defense that AI systems are incapable of having mental states"); affirmative defenses for meeting the human standard of care or pure capability failure. Resolves the FPF-identified Rhode Island gap
entry.thresholds: SB 1047's thresholds verbatim: 10²⁶ ops and >$100M compute cost; fine-tuning 3×10²⁵ ops and >$10M; also covers covered model derivatives (unmodified copies, copies with non-fine-tuning post-training changes, copies fine-tuned with ≤3×10²⁵ ops and ≤$1,000,000, copies combined with other software)

entry.title: S.10373 / A.11636 — third-party verification of RAISE compliance
entry.sponsor_text: Sen. Andrew Gounardes (D) — the RAISE Act's own sponsor
entry.mechanism: Adds new GBL §1425: large frontier developers must annually retain a third-party verifier to assess framework compliance, permissibility of redactions, and whether public statements match findings; summary published within 60 days; DFS/DIGIT to accredit verifiers by July 1, 2028 ; only accredited verifiers from Jan 1, 2029 ; AG civil penalties ($1M first/$3M subsequent) extended to §1425 violations; FOIL exemption. Sponsor memo concedes the amended RAISE Act "left a significant gap: … no mechanism exists to verify" — the sponsor re-adding the audit requirement the March 2026 chapter amendment removed Verifier gets unredacted access; payment not tied to results; report kept at least five years; summary linked developer website within fifteen days.

entry.title: S.10701 — "TERMINATOR Act" (technical evaluation, risk monitoring, incident notification, AI testing, oversight, and response act)
entry.sponsor_text: Sen. Patricia Fahy (D)
entry.mechanism: Introduced text read. Amends the RAISE Act (GBL Article 44-B as replaced by Chapter 96 of 2026) by adding GBL §§ 1430–1436 (and amending the § 1429 rulemaking section): independent pre-deployment safety evaluation of each frontier model by an accredited "independent safety evaluator" (models already deployed: within 180 days), covering underlying capabilities, capabilities reasonably accessible in the deployment configuration, and the circumvention resistance of safeguards; re-evaluation after material modifications ; post-deployment monitoring; tamper-evident safety records; rules on privileged model access and model-weight release; a duty to mitigate material and unreasonable catastrophic risk; protected safety disclosures and independent safety research, with anti-retaliation and a confidential reporting channel; "significant safety incident" reporting to the office within 7 days ; additions to transparency reports; civil penalty up to 0.5% of annual gross revenue for knowing falsification or concealment, and up to 1% for wilfully concealing a critical safety incident; no private right of action; rulemaking authority
entry.thresholds: Uses Chapter 96's existing "large frontier developer" and "frontier model" definitions (adds no compute figure)

entry.title: S.10701 — "TERMINATOR Act" (technical evaluation, risk monitoring, incident notification, AI testing, oversight, and response act)
entry.sponsor_text: Sen. Patricia Fahy (D)
entry.mechanism: Introduced text read. Amends the RAISE Act (GBL Article 44-B as replaced by Chapter 96 of 2026) by adding GBL §§ 1430–1436 (and amending the § 1429 rulemaking section): independent pre-deployment safety evaluation of each frontier model by an accredited "independent safety evaluator" (models already deployed: within 180 days), covering underlying capabilities, capabilities reasonably accessible in the deployment configuration, and the circumvention resistance of safeguards; re-evaluation after material modifications ; post-deployment monitoring; tamper-evident safety records; rules on privileged model access and model-weight release; a duty to mitigate material and unreasonable catastrophic risk; protected safety disclosures and independent safety research, with anti-retaliation and a confidential reporting channel; "significant safety incident" reporting to the office within 7 days ; additions to transparency reports; civil penalty up to 0.5% of annual gross revenue for knowing falsification or concealment, and up to 1% for wilfully concealing a critical safety incident; no private right of action; rulemaking authority

entry.title: H.B. 2800 — Artificial Intelligence Risk Prevention Act

entry.sponsor_text: Rep. Melissa Shusterman (D) with 14 Democratic co-sponsors
entry.mechanism: Introduced text read (Printer's No. 3904, 26 pp.). Free-standing act on the SB 53 pattern with a registration layer: large frontier developers file a registration form and ownership disclosure with the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency (PEMA) and pay an annual fee; publish and comply with a frontier AI framework , reviewed at least annually and re-published within 30 days of a material modification; transparency reports before deployment; annual third-party audit of compliance with this act with auditor-independence limits; critical safety incident reports to PEMA and the Attorney General within 72 hours , and within 24 hours to an appropriate authority where an incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury; whistleblower protections preserving the state Whistleblower Law; enforcement by the agency and the Attorney General with civil penalties up to $1,000,000 per violation for a first violation and $3,000,000 for a subsequent violation , plus PEMA penalties up to $1,000 per day of violation after notice and hearing, and injunctive relief
entry.thresholds: Frontier model = trained on more than 10²⁶ operations , counting the original run and subsequent fine-tuning and reinforcement learning; large frontier developer = more than $500,000,000 annual gross revenue with affiliates; catastrophic risk = death or serious injury to more than 50 people or more than $1,000,000,000 in property damage from a single incident

Free-standing act on the SB 53 pattern with a registration layer: large frontier developers file a registration form and ownership disclosure with the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency (PEMA) and pay an annual fee; publish and comply with a frontier AI framework , reviewed at least annually and re-published within 30 days of a material modification; transparency reports before deployment; annual third-party audit of compliance with this act with auditor-independence limits; critical safety incident reports to PEMA and the Attorney General within 72 hours , and within 24 hours to an appropriate authority where an incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury; whistleblower protections preserving the state Whistleblower Law; enforcement by the agency and the Attorney General with civil penalties up to $1,000,000 per violation for a first violation and $3,000,000 for a subsequent violation , plus PEMA penalties up to $1,000 per day of violation after notice and hearing, and injunctive relief
entry.thresholds: Frontier model = trained on more than 10²⁶ operations , counting the original run and subsequent fine-tuning and reinforcement learning; large frontier developer = more than $500,000,000 annual gross revenue with affiliates; catastrophic risk = death or serious injury to more than 50 people or more than $1,000,000,000 in property damage from a single incident

entry.title: H.F. 4532 / S.F. 4509 — titled the "Responsible Artificial Intelligence Safety and Education Act" (RAISE Act)
entry.sponsor_text: Rep. Jones (HF); Senate companion SF 4509
entry.mechanism: Written safety and security protocol before deployment (published, redacted copy to AG); deployment prohibited if it creates an "unreasonable risk of critical harm" ; annual protocol review; safety-incident disclosure to AG within 72 hrs; test records retained for replication; false-statement prohibition. Enforcement: AG civil penalties up to $10M first / $30M subsequent (the original NY RAISE Act figures) plus a private right of action for any injured person. Developer must retain an unredacted protocol with update records, and test records, for the entire deployment period plus five years.
entry.thresholds: No compute, cost, or revenue threshold: "developer" = any person that has trained at least one AI model. "Critical harm" = death/serious physical or mental injury of 25+ people or ≥$1,000,000 damages, via CBRN or autonomous conduct that would be an intent/recklessness/gross-negligence crime
entry.penalties: Attorney General civil penalty up to $10,000,000 for a first violation and $30,000,000 for a subsequent violation; private right of action for injured persons
entry.status_text: Status: Introduced Mar 23, 2026; referred to House Commerce Finance and Policy; no further action

entry.title: A.B. 1405 — Artificial intelligence: auditors: registration (Gov. Code §§11549.80–.86)
entry.sponsor_text: Asm. Rebecca Bauer-Kahan (D); coauthors Sens. McNerney, Rubio, Wiener
entry.mechanism: Final (Aug 25 Senate-amended, concurred Aug 30) text read. GovOps must establish an AI Auditor Registry by Jan 1, 2029 (earlier drafts said 2027); from Jan 1, 2029 no person may offer, sell, or conduct a "covered AI audit" — an audit of internal controls/processes/systems "necessary for compliance with state law" — unless registered. Registrants disclose standards applied (ISO, NIST, AICPA, etc.) and basis for validity claims; report contents specified (scope, results, deficiencies, whether auditee followed its internal safety protocols, limitations, signed statement); 10-year retention; independence rules (no self-review, no job-seeking during audit, 12-month cooling-off for former auditee staff); auditor-employee whistleblower protection; GovOps may investigate and remove from registry with referral to AG; CPA-licensed auditors deemed compliant if they follow AICPA standards; registration number on all advertising; AI Auditors' Registration Fund
entry.status_text: Status: Passed Senate Aug 30 (29–10); Assembly concurred Aug 30 (60–6) ; signed by Gov. Newsom Sept 9, 2026; chaptered as Chapter 178, Statutes of 2026. Executive Order N-9-26 (para. 2) directs GovOps, no later than Dec 1, 2027, to complete Gov. Code §11549.82(a) and begin the actions required by §11549.82(b), ahead of the statutory Jan 1, 2029 date

entry.title: H.F. 4544 / S.F. 4636 — AI independent-verification organization licensure
entry.sponsor_text: Reps. Erin Koegel (DFL), Ron Rymer (R), Matt Norris (DFL), Kristin Bahner (DFL); Sens. Nick Frentz (DFL), Eric Lucero (R)
entry.mechanism: Commerce commissioner licenses IVOs to verify risk-specific standards for any AI model/application. Applicants submit measurable risk thresholds, monitoring, mitigation, audit, corrective-action, revocation, disclosure, independence, and funding plans; licensed IVOs report annually; an independent advisory council exercises delegated licensing/auditing functions. Verification is voluntary , but verification creates a rebuttable presumption against liability for covered personal injury/property damage within the licensed risk and market

entry.title: H.F. 4544 / S.F. 4636 — AI independent-verification organization licensure
entry.sponsor_text: Reps. Erin Koegel (DFL), Ron Rymer (R), Matt Norris (DFL), Kristin Bahner (DFL); Sens. Nick Frentz (DFL), Eric Lucero (R)
entry.mechanism: Commerce commissioner licenses IVOs to verify risk-specific standards for any AI model/application. Applicants submit measurable risk thresholds, monitoring, mitigation, audit, corrective-action, revocation, disclosure, independence, and funding plans; licensed IVOs report annually; an independent advisory council exercises delegated licensing/auditing functions. Verification is voluntary , but verification creates a rebuttable presumption against liability for covered personal injury/property damage within the licensed risk and market

entry.title: S.B. 5 / Public Act 26-15 — IVO pilot program
entry.sponsor_text: Sen. Martin M. Looney (D), lead sponsor, with co-sponsors
entry.mechanism: A Department of Consumer Protection-administered IVO pilot program (Sec. 33, effective July 1, 2027) through June 30, 2030 (no more than five IVOs, each under a memorandum of understanding): IVO applications and designation standards, annual reporting, reassessment and suspension, public transparency, and rules for the evidentiary treatment of verification in private litigation (admissible solely in private personal-injury or property-damage actions; not in AG or state-agency enforcement actions, nor presumption, inference or defense there). Except: wilful, wanton or reckless conduct; misrepresentation; failure to implement corrective action. DCP must evaluate the pilot by Dec. 31, 2028 with UConn's Institute for Municipal and Regional Policy. This is an operating pilot, not merely a study. The Institute shall submit a report with the evaluation results to the joint consumer protection committee by January 31, 2029.

entry.mechanism: A Department of Consumer Protection-administered IVO pilot program (Sec. 33, effective July 1, 2027) through June 30, 2030 (no more than five IVOs, each under a memorandum of understanding): IVO applications and designation standards, annual reporting, reassessment and suspension, public transparency, and rules for the evidentiary treatment of verification in private litigation (admissible solely in private personal-injury or property-damage actions; not in AG or state-agency enforcement actions, nor presumption, inference or defense there). Except: wilful, wanton or reckless conduct; misrepresentation; failure to implement corrective action. DCP must evaluate the pilot by Dec. 31, 2028 with UConn's Institute for Municipal and Regional Policy. This is an operating pilot, not merely a study. The Institute shall submit a report with the evaluation results to the joint consumer protection committee by January 31, 2029.

entry.title: S. 2938 — Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
entry.sponsor_text: Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO), sponsor; cosponsors Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT, original) and Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN, added Mar 19, 2026)
entry.mechanism: Dept. of Energy must establish a mandatory Advanced AI Evaluation Program within 90 days: classified red-team testing, blind third-party evaluations; covered developers must participate and provide code, training data, model weights on request; no deployment unless in compliance; ≥$1M/day penalty for non-participation or deployment violations. Plan for permanent federal oversight due in 360 days, updated annually; program terminates after 7 years unless renewed by Congress. Earliest of the federal testing-mandate bills
entry.thresholds: 10²⁶ ops (Secretary may propose a new definition by rule, effective only if Congress enacts a joint resolution approving it); covers any person that designs, codes, produces, owns, or substantially modifies such a system
entry.status_text: Introduced / status: Sept 29, 2025; referred to Senate Commerce. Hearings held Sept 30, 2026 by Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs (Congress.gov actions); no further action

events.text: Introduced Sept 29, 2025; read twice and referred to Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation
events.clause: Introduced Sept 29, 2025; read twice and referred to Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation

events.text: Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) added as cosponsor Mar 19, 2026
events.clause: Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) added as cosponsor Mar 19, 2026

events.text: Hearings held Sept 30, 2026 by Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs (Congress.gov actions)
events.clause: Hearings held Sept 30, 2026 by Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs (Congress.gov actions)

framework.summary: The bill requires developers to write no safety framework or plan.

transparency_report.summary: No public report is required; the Energy program gives test reports only to participating developers.

incident_reporting.summary: Developers have no duty to report incidents to a government body.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no shorter window for imminent-risk incidents.

third_party_audit.summary: Developers must take part in the Energy Department's testing program, which uses independent third-party assessments only to the extent feasible; no private audit is required.
third_party_audit.quote: to the extent feasible, establish and facilitate classified, independent third-party assessments and blind model evaluations

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no employee protections.

registration.summary: No registration or licensing; developers must take part in the federal evaluation program and may not deploy without complying.

shutdown.summary: The Energy program must only develop recommended containment protocols; developers have no duty to build a shutdown capability.
shutdown.quote: develop recommended containment protocols, contingency planning, and mitigation strategies informed by testing data to address identified risks

compute_threshold.summary: An advanced AI system is one trained with more than 10^26 operations; the Secretary may propose a new definition only if Congress approves by joint resolution.
compute_threshold.quote: trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations

revenue_threshold.summary: Coverage does not depend on revenue, spending or users.

harm_threshold.summary: Adverse incidents are defined by type of event, with no death, injury or damage figures.

penalties.summary: A person who violates the participation or deployment rules is fined at least $1,000,000 per day of violation; the bill does not name an enforcer.
penalties.quote: shall be fined not less than $1,000,000 per day of the violation

effective_date.summary: The bill states no effective date; it sets deadlines counted from enactment.
